findings.summary: The gate compares the whole job's wall time with a deadline that applies to one run. It can refuse readings whose runs would each finish in time.
findings.evidence: outputs.rs:111 documents wall_time_s as "From dispatch to the final verdict", which covers the producer run, the verifier run and the checks. athena.toml:41-42 sets the deadlines at 3000 s and 2400 s, and each one applies to a single run. A job whose producer takes 1800 s and whose verifier takes 1200 s fits both deadlines. Its forecast p50 of about 3000 s would still be refused. The plan itself says p50 'includes the producer and the verifier' and still compares it with the smaller deadline. The rule does follow the reading the user accepted, so this is not grounds for revision. Fix: Keep the accepted rule. In the check_reading_size doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry, say that this is a conservative proxy: wall_time_s covers both runs, so the gate can refuse a reading whose runs would each fit. Name a per-run forecast split as a possible follow-up request.

findings.summary: cargo test accepts one name filter, so the first command listed would fail on its two filters.
findings.evidence: The Run line is `cargo test -p athena-core --lib a_reading_forecasting_more_than_only_the_verifier_timeout_is_refused a_reading_within_both_timeouts_is_accepted`. The plan does give an alternative afterwards: `reading::tests::a_reading_`. Fix: Use the single filter `reading::tests::a_reading_` as the main command.

findings.summary: The clippy command differs from the one the criterion names.
findings.evidence: Criterion 5 names `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`. The plan runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`. Fix: Also run the exact command the criterion names, or add `--workspace` to the plan's command.

findings.summary: The helper's signature is described two ways.
findings.evidence: Decision 1 gives the helper a has_capability parameter. Step 2 gives it (forecast, producer_timeout_s, verifier_timeout_s) and puts the capability check at the call site in Step 3. Fix: Pick one signature. Step 2/3, with the check at the call site, is fine.

summary: I read the code; I ran nothing. The plan matches the accepted reading, and the code it names exists. build_reading is at reading.rs:499 and binds `config = &jc.config` at line 512. reader.validate() is at line 542. A build_reading error becomes ReadError::Refused at line 485, so the existing correction path sends the message back to the reader. check_reading_acceptance (line 2231) has no config, so putting the gate in build_reading is where the missing comparison starts. Budget.producer_timeout_s and verifier_timeout_s are u64 fields (config.rs:232-233), and athena.toml sets them to 3000 and 2400. The test seam is real. test_support::make_athena takes (git, state_root, capabilities, Script). JobConfig's fields are public, and athena-cap-study already builds one from include_str! of athena.toml and defaults.toml. The demonstrations call the production build_reading, would fail without the gate (unwrap_err on Ok), and cover the producer-only, verifier-only, within-deadline, boundary and decline cases with generic forecasts. My search found no existing test reader with a four-digit wall_time p50, which supports the claim that existing tests are unaffected. One soundness point is minor: the gate compares the whole job's wall time with per-run deadlines. That is a conservative proxy that can refuse readings whose runs would each fit, but it is the rule the user accepted. No new config key is added, and the work fits one producer run.
